name: MS-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+21 district with the Republican incumbent renominated
Ezell's overwhelming fundraising edge ($1.09M raised vs. $60K for Hulum)
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 96 percent
No polls or expert ratings; independent evidence is thin
model.rationale: The district's twenty-one-point Republican lean, Ezell's roughly eighteen-to-one fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 96 percent Republican all point to an easy incumbent re-election, and nothing on record suggests Hulum's challenge is competitive.
model.watch: Credible polling placing Hulum within single digits, or a late surge of outside spending against Ezell, would be the main signals that could change this outlook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mississippi's fourth district, anchored along the Gulf Coast and the Pine Belt, is strongly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly twenty-one points toward the GOP. Republican incumbent Mike Ezell is seeking re-election after being renominated, and faces Democrat Jeffrey Hulum III and independent Carl Boyanton in the general election.

The evidence points firmly toward Ezell. He has raised about $1.09 million to Hulum's roughly $60,000, leaving the challenger with little money to build name recognition, and prediction markets give the Republican about a 96 percent chance of winning. No public polls or expert race ratings are available, so the outlook rests on the district's heavy Republican lean, the incumbent's financial edge, and the absence of any visible challenge infrastructure. Everything on record describes a safe Republican seat; a Hulum victory would require a dramatic, unforeseen shift.
